steps.tx: The **2012 Revised Chapel Hill Consensus Conference** or CHCC classifies systemic vasculitides based on predominant vessel caliber. Categories comprise **large vessel vasculitis** affecting aorta and major branches, **medium vessel vasculitis** targeting visceral arteries, and **small vessel vasculitis** involving intraparenchymal arterioles, capillaries, and venules.
steps.say: The Chapel Hill Consensus classifies vasculitis by predominant vessel size. Categories divide into large vessel, medium vessel, and small vessel diseases.

vis.alt: Chapel Hill Consensus Conference vessel caliber classification of systemic vasculitis
vis.caption: The Chapel Hill Consensus classifies vasculitides by vessel caliber and pathophysiology. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: Small vessel vasculitis is subdivided into pauci-immune **ANCA-associated vasculitides** and **immune complex vasculitides**. ANCA-associated vasculitides comprise microscopic polyangiitis, granulomatosis with polyangiitis, and eosinophilic GPA. Immune complex vasculitides feature antibody-antigen deposition including anti-GBM disease, cryoglobulinemic vasculitis, IgA vasculitis, and hypocomplementemic urticarial vasculitis.
steps.say: Small vessel vasculitis divides into ANCA-associated forms and immune complex diseases. Immune complex forms include anti-GBM disease, cryoglobulinemia, and IgA vasculitis.

right.title: Immune complex vasculitis
points: Abundant immunoglobulins and complement in vessel walls

steps.tx: **Variable vessel vasculitis** designates systemic disorders capable of inflaming arteries, veins, and capillaries of any caliber. The prototypical disorders are **Behcet disease**, marked by recurrent orogenital aphthae, pathergy, and uveitis, and **Cogan syndrome**, characterized by non-syphilitic interstitial keratitis, vestibuloauditory dysfunction, and aortitis.
steps.say: Variable vessel vasculitis affects blood vessels of any caliber and type. Classic prototypes include Behcet disease and Cogan syndrome.

vis.alt: Multisystem variable caliber vascular inflammation in Behcet disease
vis.caption: Variable-vessel vasculitis damages arteries, veins, and microvasculature. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: **Single-organ vasculitis** or SOV is necrotizing vasculitis confined to arteries or veins within an isolated organ without systemic involvement. Prototypic examples include **primary angiitis of the central nervous system**, cutaneous leukocytoclastic angiitis, isolated testicular vasculitis, and isolated coronary arteritis, requiring rigorous systemic exclusion.
steps.say: Single-organ vasculitis affects vessels within one organ without systemic disease. Examples include primary CNS angiitis and isolated cutaneous vasculitis.

nodes.label: Localized vasculitic injury demonstrated on tissue biopsy
Exclusion of systemic constitutional and multiorgan signs
Classification as single-organ vasculitis (PACNS, cutaneous angiitis)

steps.tx: Secondary vasculitis arises from defined etiologies or underlying systemic conditions. Recognized categories include vasculitis associated with systemic diseases such as **lupus vasculitis**, **rheumatoid vasculitis**, and sarcoidosis. In contrast, vasculitis with probable etiology encompasses **hepatitis B-associated polyarteritis nodosa** and **hepatitis C-associated cryoglobulinemia**.
steps.say: Secondary vasculitides develop from underlying infections or autoimmune diseases. Examples include hepatitis B-related PAN and hepatitis C cryoglobulinemia.

steps.tx: The **2022 ACR/EULAR classification criteria** provide validated scoring systems for five primary vasculitides: GPA, MPA, EGPA, Takayasu arteritis, and giant cell arteritis. These modern criteria incorporate surrogate imaging, ANCA antibody specificity by immunoassay, and detailed clinical features with weighted points and validated diagnostic thresholds.
steps.say: The 2022 ACR/EULAR criteria provide modern weighted scoring sets for primary vasculitides. They incorporate specific ANCA immunoassays and advanced vascular imaging.

steps.tx: Vasculitis disease activity is prospectively measured using the **Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score** or BVAS version 3 across 64 defined items in nine organ systems. BVAS captures active, new, or worsening reversible inflammation, rigorously distinguishing acute disease activity from irreversible permanent damage measured by the **Vasculitis Damage Index** or VDI.
steps.say: The Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score quantifies reversible active disease across nine organ domains, while the Vasculitis Damage Index tracks permanent damage.

left.title: BVAS (Activity score)
points: Scores only new or worsening manifestations

right.title: VDI (Damage index)
points: Can only remain stable or increase over time

steps.tx: The revised **Five-Factor Score** predicts 5-year mortality in necrotizing systemic vasculitides including PAN, MPA, and EGPA. The 5 adverse prognostic factors comprise **age over 65 years**, cardiac involvement, gastrointestinal ischemia, renal insufficiency with serum creatinine **150 micromol/L or higher**, and the absence of ENT symptoms.
steps.say: The Five-Factor Score predicts mortality in necrotizing vasculitis. Scoring factors include age over 65, cardiac, gastrointestinal, and renal involvement.
